name: SONF compliance kit for law firms, accountants and other non-financial obliged subjects (SSNF self-assessment, registration, UAF reports)
buyer: Small law firms, accounting offices, corredores and other SONF registered with SSNF (about 12,000 SONF, more than 60% lawyers)
trigger: Ley 124/2020 (SSNF); Res. S-010-2021 (online registration app); Res. S-022-2025 of 21 Mar 2025 requires risk self-assessment questionnaires; SSNF may request client/operation data (art. 43 as amended by Ley 254/2021); fine $5,000 for not registering; UAF reports via secure platform with ADSO code.
existing: Competitor search (software cumplimiento SSNF sujetos obligados no financieros) found no dedicated product; results were only SSNF notices and press. KPMG publishes an SONF obligations guide (consulting, not software). Large-firm compliance software and consultants probably exist; not confirmed.
unchecked: Whether SSNF app already pre-fills the self-assessment; the actual periodic deadlines for the questionnaire; how many small offices use outside compliance officers; overlap with K01 buyer lists.

first_check.duty: Ley 23 of 2015 and DE 35/2022, plus Acuerdo JD-02-2022 for lawyers and accountants: client due diligence, beneficial-owner identification, risk-based matrix, prevention manual, UAF liaison and reports, and an annual update of high-risk client files (per the KPMG guide). Ley 124/2020 requires SSNF registration, with a $5,000 fine for resident agents who don't register. Res. S-022-2025 of 21 Mar 2025, published in Gaceta Oficial 30248 on 1 Apr 2025, requires the self-assessment questionnaires. The questionnaire's periodicity and deadline could not be confirmed: the PDF was too large to fetch. Sanctions are reported at USD 5,000 to 5 million (Chambers).
first_check.market: About 12,000 sujetos obligados no financieros were registered with the SSNF over 2020-2024, more than 60% of them lawyers (La Estrella, 24 Mar 2025). A separate count of 7,500 resident agents is cited in the same article. Earlier SSNF data show 664 law firms and 2,271 individual lawyers registered (as of 2022).
first_check.competitor: No dedicated Panamanian product for SONF compliance (SSNF registration, the questionnaire, the risk matrix and UAF reporting) was found in Spanish or English searches. The free SSNF online app (Res. S-010-2021) handles registration and probably the questionnaire submission; that is unconfirmed. Generic AML/KYC screening vendors pitch Panama (Didit's AML screening API, Sanction Scanner). Consultants offer guidance, for example KPMG's SONF obligations guide. Outsourced compliance-officer services were not checked (not_reached).
first_check.reason: The duty is real and current. Ley 23/2015, Ley 124/2020 (the SSNF law, art. 43 amended by Ley 254/2021), DE 35/2022 and Acuerdo JD-02-2022 put KYC, a risk matrix, a prevention manual and UAF reporting on lawyers and accountants. Res. S-022-2025 (Gaceta 30248, 1 Apr 2025) adds risk self-assessment questionnaires. About 12,000 SONF are registered, over 60% of them lawyers. No Panama-specific SONF compliance software turned up; I found only generic KYC/screening APIs (Didit, Sanction Scanner) and Big-4 guides. The catch is that registration and the questionnaire are filed free through the SSNF online app. The paid value would be ongoing due diligence and the risk matrix, which is closer to generic KYC tooling. The questionnaire frequency is unverified. Small firms are price-sensitive, and some lawyers are giving up resident-agent work instead of complying.

challenge_check.killer: No killer. AgileCheck Express is a partial competitor (screening and risk matrix only). Not verified: the scope of the free SSNF app and the questionnaire deadlines.
challenge_check.reason: Nothing I found does the whole job. AgileCheck Express is the closest partial competitor: its Software Advice/GetApp listings say it covers Panama's SSNF and sells to law firms, accountants and realtors on per-use credits, with sanctions/PEP screening and a weighted risk matrix. But the vendor's own site is aimed at Venezuela and does not mention the SSNF questionnaire, registration or UAF reports. Didit and Shufti only do screening. The duty is getting stricter: Res. S-008-2026 requires enhanced due diligence on PEPs, and a sworn statement under JD-02-2022 was due 1 Dec 2025. The market may be smaller than claimed, since lawyers are dropping the resident-agent role because SSNF and UAF compliance costs more than it earns. The free SSNF app's scope and the questionnaire deadlines are still unverified.
